example_file_as_shipped.yaml:
# Custom grade thresholds for epochix.
#
# Copy this file to the folder you run epochix from, name it `.epochix.yaml`,
# and uncomment the entries you want to change. As it stands it changes
# nothing: every entry is commented out.
#
# Where it is looked for: the current folder, then each parent, then
# ~/.epochix/.epochix.yaml. EPOCHIX_GRADE_CONFIG names a file directly, or
# turns the lookup off with `off`. `epochix check <log>` says which file is in
# use and whether it applies to that log.
#
# Reference: https://epochix.dev/config/

version: 1

# ── Grade thresholds ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# An entry lists, for each grade, the lowest value that still earns it — or the
# highest, for a metric where lower is better. The order of the numbers says
# which: write them from A+ down to F and epochix reads the direction from
# them. You do not have to list every grade.
#
# A TASK entry applies to one metric of that task, named beside it below. A
# run told by another metric is not touched by it.
#
# A METRIC entry (the name of a metric instead of a task) applies to that
# metric in any run. Use it for a metric that has no entry of its own.
#
# The values below are the built-in ones, so uncommenting an entry without
# editing it changes nothing.

grade_thresholds:

  # classification:         # applies to: val_accuracy, accuracy
  #   "A+": 0.95
  #   A:    0.90
  #   "A-": 0.87
  #   "B+": 0.82
  #   B:    0.75
  #   "B-": 0.70
  #   "C+": 0.65
  #   C:    0.60
  #   "C-": 0.55
  #   D:    0.50
  #   F:    0.0

  # detection:              # applies to: mAP50
  #   "A+": 0.75
  #   A:    0.65
  #   "A-": 0.58
  #   "B+": 0.50
  #   B:    0.42
  #   "B-": 0.35
  #   "C+": 0.28
  #   C:    0.20
  #   "C-": 0.15
  #   D:    0.08
  #   F:    0.0

  # segmentation:           # applies to: mIoU
  #   "A+": 0.85
  #   A:    0.78
  #   "A-": 0.72
  #   "B+": 0.66
  #   B:    0.60
  #   "B-": 0.54
  #   "C+": 0.47
  #   C:    0.40
  #   "C-": 0.32
  #   D:    0.20
  #   F:    0.0

  # nlp:                    # applies to: perplexity (lower is better)
  #   "A+": 10.0
  #   A:    20.0
  #   "A-": 30.0
  #   "B+": 50.0
  #   B:    80.0
  #   "B-": 120.0
  #   "C+": 180.0
  #   C:    250.0
  #   "C-": 350.0
  #   D:    500.0
  #   F:    .inf

  # biometric:              # applies to: EER (lower is better)
  #   "A+": 0.01
  #   A:    0.03
  #   "A-": 0.05
  #   "B+": 0.08
  #   B:    0.10
  #   "B-": 0.15
  #   "C+": 0.20
  #   C:    0.25
  #   "C-": 0.30
  #   D:    0.40
  #   F:    .inf

  # gaze:                   # applies to: val_MAE, MAE in degrees (lower is better)
  #   "A+": 0.5
  #   A:    1.0
  #   "A-": 1.5
  #   "B+": 2.5
  #   B:    4.0
  #   "B-": 6.0
  #   "C+": 9.0
  #   C:    12.0
  #   "C-": 16.0
  #   D:    22.0
  #   F:    .inf

  # ── No built-in thresholds: these change how the run is graded ────────────
  #
  # By default an MAE, an FID and a metric epochix does not recognise are
  # graded on how far they improved, because a log cannot say what a good
  # value is. Writing thresholds here supplies that, in your own units. The
  # numbers below are placeholders — replace them with yours.

  # regression:             # applies to: val_MAE, MAE (not R2, which has its own)
  #   A: 1.0
  #   B: 2.5
  #   C: 5.0
  #   D: 10.0
  #   F: .inf

  # generative:             # applies to: fid
  #   A: 10.0
  #   B: 40.0
  #   C: 130.0
  #   D: 300.0
  #   F: .inf

  # custom:                 # applies to whatever a run with no known task is told by
  #   A: 0.90
  #   B: 0.75
  #   C: 0.60
  #   D: 0.50
  #   F: 0.0

  # ── A metric entry ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  #
  # F1 is graded on accuracy's bands by default. This gives it bands of its
  # own — lower ones, say, where the positive class is rare.

  # val_f1:
  #   A: 0.90
  #   B: 0.75
  #   C: 0.60
  #   D: 0.50
  #   F: 0.0

# ── Direction ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Only for a metric whose name does not say which way is better. epochix knows
# that a loss or an error falls and an accuracy rises; for a name it does not
# recognise in a run with no known task, it assumes higher is better unless
# told otherwise here.

# lower_better:
#   custom: true

grade_thresholds:

    C:    0.75
    D:    0.60
    F:    0.0

    B: 0.75
    C: 0.60
    F: 0.0
